To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the Wagner model is applicable to bodies moving in more than six d.f., that the Wagner model can be applied to bodies that deform over time and that the Wagner model may be used to determine the occurrence of low pressures during the water entry process.

a smooth body can move freely and can also change its shape in 6 d.f., during the water impact, the water entry problem can be reduced to a vertical entry problem with modified vertical displacement of a body, low pressure occurrence can precede appearance of cavitation, the low pressure can be predicted by the Wagner theory and hydrodynamic forces can be analysed for a rigid body with 3 d.o.f. the water entry of an arbitrary body is reduced to that of a body with vertical motion; the low pressure region can precede the cavitation region; the hydrodynamic loads are determined by the Wagner theory; the hydrodynamic pressure is calculated for the case of a rigid ellipsoid; the hydrodynamic force is calculated for the oblique impact of an elliptic paraboloids.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the hydrodynamics of a three-dimensional body entering a liquid.
the problem of water impact of a body moving in more than six d.f. and changing its shape over time, which is of interest in many practical situations.
the hydrodynamic loads on a body entering the water at an arbitrary angle and with arbitrary kinematics.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the model presented here is a very useful tool for the analysis of the water entry problem.
the water entry of bodies with 3 d.o.f. can be analysed by a simple and efficient method, which can be used in the analysis of water entry of bodies in real life.
the water entry of a body, which moves in more then six degrees of freedom, can be analysed by Wagner theory.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a general theory for the water entry of a body that can move freely in all its 6 d. f.
the water entry of a 3D body with 6 d.f is equivalent to the entry of a 2D body with 2 d.f.
the water entry of bodies moving in 6 d.f can be reduced to that of vertical impact with a modified vertical position of the body and a contact region of elliptic shape.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the water entry of a body with 6 d.f., which is allowed to change shape during penetration, can be reduced in its mathematical formulation to the water entry of an elliptic paraboloidal body.
the Wagner model is valid for a wide range of impact velocities and can be used to predict the hydrodynamic loads for the entry of a three dimensional body.
the water entry of a deformable body is not a new problem, but can be treated as a special case of the water entry of rigid bodies.
